name: plumbing_iterator_after_pass
description: Test 25 (PL4; hand-derived from 6.6, 9 field 14 and simgrid 7.4): the scanning iterator's GetNext after the last cell sets x := x0 = 0 and z := z + 1 = countZ, finds z > z1 and becomes done, so it rests at (0, countZ), not (0, countZ - 1). 64 x 64 city, pump of 1000 at (5,5) (water at (5,4)). Init creates it fresh at (0,0) over [0,63]^2, step 1. State 2 resets it to (0,0) and scans every cell with it, so after the first three DoIdle calls (states 0, 1, 2) it is done at (0, 64) even on the first pass. State 3 seeds the pump (state 4); state 4 returns to 3; the nothing-left branch of state 3 resets it to (0,0), fresh. State 5 falls through into state 6, which resets it again at its end (fresh at (0,0), state 7). State 7 does not reset it and leaves it done at (0, 64); state 8 does not touch it. A save now holds field 14 = 02, x 0, z 64, step 1, rectangle 0, 0, 63, 63, at offset 2 + 16 + 8 + 4096 + 4 + 4 + 8 + 4 + 4 + 40 (one producer) + 36 (null current) = 4222. Write -> Read -> Write is byte-identical; the loaded iterator is the saved one (Init leaves it, 4.1 step 4 is skipped), and the next pass runs normally: state 2 resets and rescans it, the pass publishes the pump lot (5,5) = 7 (watered 1 | lot 2 | producer only 4), and it ends done at (0, 64) again. A 64 x 32 city (no buildings) ends its pass with the iterator done at (0, 32) over [0,63] x [0,31], also when states 6 and 7 are sliced to 500 cells per call.
